name: Sheshbazzar
overview: Sheshbazzar is identified in Scripture as the prince or governor of Judah appointed by King Cyrus to lead the return of the Jewish exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem. He was entrusted with the sacred task of bringing back the gold and silver vessels taken from the temple by Nebuchadnezzar, demonstrating God's providence in preserving what was holy. Additionally, Sheshbazzar laid the foundation of the temple in Jerusalem, marking the beginning of its restoration, though the work remained unfinished at that time. Some biblical scholars suggest that Sheshbazzar may be another name for Zerubbabel, linking these leaders in the post-exilic rebuilding effort.
